title: Inverse problem: permittivity of a slab from its reflection spectrum (1D)
description: A dielectric slab of unknown permittivity and loss is measured in reflection: the 'measurement' is a 1-D FDTD run (with the CPML, the scheme's dispersion and added receiver noise), the model is the transfer-matrix reflection of pp.em.waves.multilayer. Least squares recovers eps_r and the conductivity with their covariance; the recovered values are compared with the truth the measurement was generated from (hidden from the fit), and the fit is repeated on noise realisations to check the stated uncertainty.

metrics.name: rel_error[1D: eps_r recovered vs truth]
metrics.how: |computed - reference| / |reference| (ground_truth: the permittivity the FDTD measurement was generated with (hidden from the fit))

metrics.name: 1D: eps_r_recovered
metrics.how: least squares on the noisy FDTD reflection spectrum

metrics.name: 1D: model_error_max
metrics.how: max |r_FDTD - r_model| at the true parameters (no noise)

metrics.name: 1D: coverage_2u_eps
metrics.how: fraction of 100 noise realisations within 2 u

checks.name: [1D] eps_r recovered vs truth
checks.detail: the permittivity the FDTD measurement was generated with (hidden from the fit)
checks.label: eps_r recovered vs truth vs ground truth

checks.name: [1D] sigma recovered vs truth
checks.label: sigma recovered vs truth vs ground truth

checks.name: [1D] FDTD measurement and transfer-matrix model agree below the noise
[1D] stated u(eps) consistent with the scatter (std of z between 0.7 and 1.5)
checks.detail: z = (eps_fit - eps_true) / u(eps_fit); its std is 1 when u is right (a bias from the FDTD-vs-model difference shows as a shift)

references: Baker-Jarvis et al., NIST Technical Note 1536 (2004), transmission/reflection methods
Born & Wolf, Principles of Optics, 7th ed., sec. 1.6 (characteristic matrices)
